text:
Incident Bot: PAGERDUTY -> HIGH: multiple 429 / authz errors from Stripe when acknowledging webhooks. Error rate spiked ~07:12 UTC, automated retries are backing up our webhook queue. Potential billing/quota enforcement from Stripe.

Maya: saw the page, I'm on it. Initial impact: webhook acks failing -> downstream payment status updates delayed. Visible in /payments/ingest with backlog growing.

Ash: logs show `stripe_gateway.ack` returning `429: rate_limit` with body `{"error": {"type": "rate_limit", "message": "Too many requests"}}`. Spike started 07:10 UTC, traffic pattern normal.

Lex: are these 429s from our webhook endpoints to Stripe (outbound) or Stripe to us (inbound)?

Ash: outbound to Stripe when we call their `/v1/webhooks/ack` (internal name) to confirm delivery -> we're getting throttled. Inbound webhooks from Stripe are fine, it's our calls to confirm resends & billing ack that are failing.

Kevin: ok, that maps to the billing sync step. If Stripe is throttling ack calls they're probably enforcing merchant-level quota. Could be a billing enforcement window. Check account IDs in the failing payloads.

Maya: confirmed failing account IDs: acct_89f... and acct_12c... (enterprise customers). 429s have header `Stripe-Rate-Limit: account_quota`.

Sam: tagging Billing: @Billing Bot can you confirm whether we've had any invoice/plan issues with these merchants? Also filing support with Stripe now — I'll include request IDs.

Billing Bot: Received. Opening internal ticket BI-5429 to track customer-facing escalation and whether to offer manual bill credits.

Maya: mitigation proposals: 1) enable polling fallback for affected merchants (switch webhook delivery to polling for 30m) 2) apply temporary per-account circuit-breaker to stop ack retries and avoid further throttling 3) open support case with Stripe and request quota bump or guidance.

Lex: I can flip the polling flag per-merchant via the ops shim: 
``` 
POST /ops/feature-flags/polling
{ "merchant_ids": ["acct_89f...","acct_12c..."], "enable": true, "ttl_minutes": 30 }
```
I'll queue that, but need someone to own the rollback.

Ash: recommend circuit-breaker first to stop the retry storms. We have `stripe_ack_circuit_{merchant_id}` in Redis; toggle to `open` will stop attempts. Command: `redis-cli SET stripe_ack_circuit:acct_89f... open EX 1800`.

Kevin: do we have any customers already complaining? Any visible 503s or timeouts on checkout flows?

Maya: we have two support tickets flagged as payment-not-processed, both from EU merchants. Severity for customers is medium (delayed payments). Not blocking all traffic.

Sam: I started a support ticket with Stripe: https://support.stripe.com/tickets/TS-90123 (include request_id list: r_1723xx, r_1724yy). I'm also DMing our Stripe CSM.

Ops Bot: Automated action: enabled queue-backlog-mode for `webhook-processor` at 07:20 UTC to avoid OOMs. Slow consumer metrics rising.

Lex: I'm enabling polling fallback now and applying circuit-breaker to the two merchant accounts. Executing commands.

Lex: done. Polling flag enabled for acct_89f... acct_12c... Circuit-breakers set to open in Redis. Backlog still draining but retries stopped.

Ash: logs show no further `stripe_gateway.ack` retries for those merchant IDs. Error rate dropped ~07:28 UTC.

Maya: customer impact assessment: intermittent delays to invoice/charge status for two enterprise merchants. No data loss; events queued and will be processed once Stripe lifts quota or we resume ack flow. Recommend S2 and customer comms via support.

Kevin: next steps: 1) escalate with Stripe CSM for quota detail and expected window 2) keep circuit-breakers in place until we confirm quota lift 3) prepare rollback plan to restore ack path and disable polling per-merchant 4) update customers via support with ETA and compensation if needed.

Sam: I posted an update to the impacted customers and asked support to mark as incident-related. Going to request Slack status blurb if ACME (acct_89f...) requests it.

Maya: handing off on-call to Lex for the bridge — Lex, you now own the incident. I'll remain available for runbook items. Planning a 15-min bridge to monitor Stripe response.

Lex: on it. Starting bridge in #incident-bridge in 5. Paging Stripe CSM again.

Incident Bot: NOTE: created incident ticket INF-2025-87, severity S2, postmortem required.

Ops Bot: Reminder: if polling fallback causes higher token costs, Redwood Optimize should be consulted for temporary cost cap settings.

Kevin: once Stripe confirms quota lift, we need to perform a staged re-enable: 1) disable circuit-breaker 2) re-enable a single merchant ack for smoke 3) monitor error rates and token consumption 4) rollback if 429s recur.

Lex: acknowledged. I'll run the staged restore and paste runbook steps in the bridge.

Maya: thanks team. Leaving thread.

Lex: updating thread: Stripe CSM replied at 07:45 UTC — they confirm account-level rate enforcement due to automated billing retries from the merchants. Stripe suggested throttling on our side and requested request_id list; also provided temporary window estimate ~30-60m. They've assigned internal ticket STR-5582.

Sam: Stripe asked for sample `request_id` and timestamp logs — I've attached `r_1723xx` and `r_1724yy` and logs to their portal.

Lex: after ~30m, error rate back down to baseline. I'll keep circuit-breakers open for a full hour and then coordinate staged re-enable.

Incident Bot: SEVERITY DOWNGRADED -> S3 at 08:12 UTC. Monitoring. Postmortem deadline: 2025-05-10.

Lex: handing back sleep to Maya at 08:15 UTC. Closing bridge but keeping thread pinned until postmortem created.

Maya: thanks all. Postmortem owner: Ash.

Ash: ack, will start draft and include timeline, root cause (merchant-initiated retry storm + Stripe account-level quota), mitigations (polling fallback, circuit-breaker), and follow-ups (improve retry backoff, add per-merchant rate controller).

Incident Bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: snapshot recorded in INF-2025-87.
